mathematical_definitions: Fin n is the n-element vertex type consisting of indices 0 through n - 1.
The admissible parameter type is the subtype of real p satisfying 0 <= p <= 1.
The binomial random graph law is the displayed measure on simple graphs induced from a Bernoulli measure on allowable unordered nonloop edges through the graph edge-set representation.
The degree of a vertex in a finite simple graph is the cardinality of its neighbor set.
The canonical model object is the two-component package whose first component is the binomial random graph measure and whose second component is ordinary graph degree.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural number n and every real p in [0,1], the canonical packaged graph model on the n-element vertex set has graph law exactly the binomial random graph measure with parameter p, and its degree operation agrees, for every vertex and every simple graph on that vertex set, with the usual graph-theoretic degree. Both assertions are definitional consequences of how the package is constructed.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement permits n = 0. In that case there is no vertex v in Fin 0, so the universally quantified degree conjunct is vacuous, although the graph-law equality remains asserted.
